messages:
lina: Quick thread about canary/A-B guardrails after yesterday's outage. Want to pin down decision boundaries and operational flow.

noah: Short summary: probes -> score per window -> decision. But we need deterministic tie-breakers when signals disagree.

triage-bot: incident bot: alert: service=embedder region=eu-west spike in p99 latency -> 5xxs 02:14 UTC

oscar: Tie-breakers idea: priority ordering of signals. e.g., safety_signals = [sev1_errors, quality_delta, latency_p99, error_rate]. Any sev1 in window => immediate rollback. Otherwise compare weighted score.

dev: We should include an operator override TTL so manual rollbacks by oncall don't get stomped by autopilot re-applies. TTL example: 30m.

lina: Thinking about interfaces: decision engine exposes REST /v1/verdicts POST {canary_id, window_start, aggregated_signals} -> {verdict, reason, suggested_percent}. Router subscribes to verdicts via push webhook.

noah: Also surface minimal diagnostics: top contributing signals + small histogram. Keep payload < 2KB.

oscar: Cache-locality note: If we switch from v1->v2 for cohort, we ought to keep the cohort fraction sticky per user-id hash for at least 1 hour to preserve cache warmth.

triage-bot: deploy bot: canary deploy started service=embedder cohort=3% @lina

dev: For rollout ramp-down, prefer a staged decay: 3% -> 1% -> 0 over 2m. Instant 0 is fine for Sev1.

lina: I can prototype the verdict API + a tiny UI that shows recent windows and diagnostics. Who can help instrument aggregator?

noah: I'll handle aggregator + sampling. Keep sampling stratified by tenant size.

oscar: I'll work on router consumer (webhook + local cache).

lina: cool. Will file a RFC draft with the API shape and operator flows. Aim to have a working prototype next week.

dev: +1
